NP Presspad 1.1.11 — Tighter connection security

Housekeeping on how the app talks to your WordPress sites. Nothing to do after updating unless you sync a site over an unencrypted connection, in which case see below.

## What's new for you

- **HTTPS is now enforced on every request, not just when you add a site.** The check used to happen when a site was saved or its connection tested. Everything else — pulling posts, pushing edits, uploading media — trusted whatever address was already stored. Any site saved before the rule existed kept syncing unencrypted, password included. Every request is now checked before it leaves your machine.
- **Redirects can no longer quietly downgrade a connection.** A site that redirects from `https://` to `http://` used to be followed without comment. The app now checks each hop and refuses the downgrade.
- **Clearer rules for local development sites.** Anything on `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` stays unrestricted — that traffic never leaves your computer. A site on a network address such as `mysite.local` does put its password on your network in the clear, so it now asks you to tick **Allow unencrypted connection** for that site. Sites you already had set up keep working untouched; you'll only see this when adding or editing one.

## Also fixed

- **A date field could blank out the whole Custom Fields panel.** If a date value on the site wasn't stored in the exact format the app expected, rendering the panel threw and took every field with it. Unrecognised dates now show as "Pick a date" instead.

Public sites still require `https://` and always will, regardless of that setting.

No dependency changes in this release.
